title: Count Triplets That Can Form Two Arrays of Equal XOR
summary: Given an array of integers arr, find the number of triplets (i, j, k) where 0 <= i < j <= k < arr.length, such that the bitwise XOR of elements from index i to j-1 equals the bitwise XOR of elements from index j to k.
statement: Given an array of integers arr, find the number of triplets (i, j, k) where 0 <= i < j <= k < arr.length, such that the bitwise XOR of elements from index i to j-1 equals the bitwise XOR of elements from index j to k.
constraints: Count triples i<j<=k where XOR(arr[i:j]) equals XOR(arr[j:k+1]).
Different j values count as different triples.
hints: The two segment XORs are equal exactly when the XOR from i through k is zero.
For each start i, extend k while maintaining that range XOR.
A zero-XOR range of length k-i+1 permits every j from i+1 through k, giving k-i triples.
This equivalence removes the need to inspect j separately.
editorial: This equivalence removes the need to inspect j separately.

tests.explanation: Four triples split zero-XOR ranges at their valid internal positions.
Ten triples satisfy the equal-XOR condition.
